description: A six-panel composite figure (2 x 3 layout) combining one BSE-SEM micrograph with five EPMA elemental maps of the same field in an SPSed Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 high-entropy steel. Top-left: BSE image with a 50 µm scale bar, showing a light grey matrix with evenly scattered dark grey angular particles; two circles annotated "2" (left) and "1" (right) mark the WDS analysis spots. The other panels are EPMA maps labelled Fe (top-middle), Mn (top-right), Si (bottom-left), Ni (bottom-middle) and Al (bottom-right), each with a vertical colour bar printed only as E-notation numbers (Fe 1.4E1-2.0E2; Mn 7.1E1-7.9E2; Al 3.2E1-6.1E2; Si 8.0E0-1.6E2; Ni 0.0E0-~4.7E1) with no stated unit. Fe is uniformly high (red/orange) across the whole field; Mn is intermediate (blue/green); Ni is uniformly low (dark blue); Si is low with a few brighter islands. Al is strongly heterogeneous, forming a patchy high-intensity (orange/red) network against green lower-intensity regions. Together the panels show micron-scale homogeneity of Fe, Mn and Ni with clear Al (and local Si) segregation, supporting a multiphase microstructure.

subfigures.description: BSE-SEM micrograph of the SPSed sample with a 50 µm scale bar; light grey matrix containing evenly distributed dark grey angular particles. Two circles are annotated '2' (left) and '1' (right), marking the point WDS analysis locations. The contrast difference between the two circled spots is not clearly discernible at the supplied resolution.

EPMA map labelled 'Fe': nearly uniform high X-ray intensity (red/orange) over the entire field with only minor darker mottling; colour bar tick labels read 1.4E1 at the bottom to 2.0E2 at the top, no unit stated.
EPMA map labelled 'Mn': intermediate-intensity blue/green mottled distribution, with small brighter green/yellow flecks; colour bar tick labels from 7.1E1 to 7.9E2, no unit stated.
EPMA map labelled 'Si': overall low blue/green intensity with a few isolated brighter (green/yellow) islands; colour bar tick labels from 8.0E0 to 1.6E2, no unit stated.
EPMA map labelled 'Ni': uniformly low, dark blue/navy intensity over the whole field with fine speckle; colour bar tick labels from 0.0E0 to approximately 4.7E1, only partially readable.
EPMA map labelled 'Al': strongly heterogeneous, patchy high-intensity orange/red network with lower-intensity green regions; colour bar tick labels from 3.2E1 to 6.1E2, no unit stated.

observations.observation: The figure is a 2 x 3 composite of six panels: one BSE-SEM micrograph plus five EPMA elemental maps labelled Fe, Mn, Ni, Si and Al; all panels cover the same field of view.
The BSE micrograph carries a 50 µm scale bar and is annotated with two circles labelled '2' (left) and '1' (right); the matrix is light grey with evenly scattered dark grey angular particles.
The Fe map is almost uniformly high in intensity (red/orange) over the whole field, with a colour bar spanning about 1.4E1 to 2.0E2.
The Al map is strongly heterogeneous: high-intensity orange/red regions form a patchy network against lower-intensity green regions (colour bar ~3.2E1 to 6.1E2).
The Ni map is uniformly low-intensity dark blue across the field (colour bar roughly 0.0E0 to 4.7E1), and the Si map is low with a few isolated brighter islands (colour bar 8.0E0 to 1.6E2).
None of the five colour bars carries a stated unit or signal quantity; only E-notation tick numbers are printed.
The caption states the figure is a BSE image and EPMA elemental mapping of the SPSed sample.
The citing text states that point WDS analysis of the white contrast region (spot 1) is rich in Al and Ni and corresponds to the B2-type phase.
The citing text states that the light grey contrast region (spot 2) is rich in Fe, Mn and Ni and corresponds to the BCC (ferritic) phase.
The citing text states that Fe, Mn and Ni are almost uniformly distributed in the matrix owing to the major BCC phase, matching the uniform Fe/Mn/Ni maps seen here.
The citing text states that the high X-ray intensity regions corresponding to Al also show slightly higher Fe and Ni intensity, attributed to the B2-type phase.

The citing text states that the Si-enriched region indicates an Fe-Si-type phase, and that gamma-brass-type phase regions are difficult to distinguish in the maps, consistent with the low gamma-brass phase fraction found by XRD.
The citing text states that the elemental weight percentages from point WDS are listed in Table 5, which is not part of this figure group.

The three BSE contrast levels named in the citing text (white, light grey, evenly distributed dark grey particles) are consistent with the grey matrix and dark particles visible in the micrograph, but the white/light-grey distinction is not resolvable at the supplied image resolution.
